hero_headline: AI stocks whipsaw on midterm regulation fear while copper and central bank gold flash physical tightness
daily_overview: Markets spent the week pricing political risk into AI. US midterm results left Democrats dominant, and investors initially read that as slower permitting, tighter model rules and a higher hurdle rate for data center capex, wiping trillions from AI-linked market values before buyers stepped back in on Friday. The physical economy is telling a different story: Trafigura is buying copper aggressively into Asia as Chinese supply runs short and spot premiums print records, while China's central bank extended its gold-buying streak to two years even as bullion slid roughly 7 percent below the $4,000 an ounce level. Both are reserve and inventory decisions, not momentum trades. In tech, agent infrastructure is the quiet theme: Vercel shipped a browser-automation CLI for AI agents, Cloudflare published a machine-verifiable security-audit skill, and OpenAI detailed a 100-task benchmark for wet-lab science agents, evidence the tooling layer is maturing faster than the evaluation layer. Overseas, New Zealand's election heads to a minor-party kingmaker, Paraguay's president was impeached and placed under house arrest after a bank collapse, and Europe is contending with coordinated bomb threats and cyberattacks. The through-line for US traders: political outcomes are now a direct input into AI capex timelines, while metals are pricing real scarcity.

tech_briefs.title: China's central bank extends gold buying to a second year as bullion slips below $4,000
tech_briefs.summary: China's central bank bought gold for a 24th consecutive month in October, the same month bullion fell almost 7 percent and lost the $4,000 an ounce handle. Sovereign reserve managers are not momentum buyers; they are rebalancing reserve stacks away from dollar assets. Price weakness is their discount, not their signal. Not financial advice. Views are my own.

tech_briefs.title: Texas data center buildout faces political risk after Democratic midterm gains
tech_briefs.summary: Mechanism worth watching: a Democratic sweep raises the odds of AI regulation, which raises the hurdle rate on data center capex. Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market, is directly exposed if state incentives shift. That flows into the order books of electrical and site-infrastructure contractors before it hits hyperscaler earnings. Watch backlog guidance, not tweets. Not financial advice. Views are my own.

tech_briefs.title: Trafigura builds copper positions in Asia as Chinese spot supply tightens
tech_briefs.summary: Copper spot premiums in Asia are at records as Trafigura loads up and Chinese local supply tightens. That is a physical-market signal, not a futures one, and it usually leads equity narratives by a quarter or two. Full breakdown of the flows and which miners carry leverage is in the link in my bio. If copper holds these premiums into Q1, do you buy the miners or the metal? Not financial advice. Views are my own.

finance_briefs.title: AI shares rebound after midterm-driven selloff erased trillions in market value
finance_briefs.summary: AI-linked stocks recovered part of steep losses after investors sold on fears that Democratic election gains would slow AI development and invite tighter regulation. The rebound suggests positioning, not fundamentals, drove the drawdown. Analysts note concern about AI capex returns had been building before the vote, so the political catalyst amplified an existing debate rather than creating it. (multiple reports)

finance_briefs.title: Markets weigh whether divided politics slows the AI capital spending cycle
finance_briefs.summary: Investors are modeling Democratic dominance as a drag on the AI boom, citing permitting friction, energy policy and regulatory scrutiny of large platforms. Coverage contrasts that with voter hostility to Big Tech in the US and markedly more optimistic attitudes in Asia. The market question is whether political risk changes announced capex or only the multiple applied to it.

finance_briefs.title: Indebted tycoons leave China's lenders with a lasting credit hangover
finance_briefs.summary: Chinese banks are still absorbing losses from years of aggressive corporate lending to highly leveraged founders and conglomerates. The piece frames the problem as a slow workout rather than a single shock, with provisioning and hidden exposure determining how quickly credit can be redirected to policy priorities. That constraint matters for any stimulus transmission into real activity.

finance_briefs.title: Copper scramble deepens as Trafigura lifts spot buying into short Asian market
finance_briefs.summary: Trafigura has been buying large copper volumes to boost sales into Asia as local supplies run low, pushing regional premiums for spot cargoes to record highs. Physical tightness of this kind typically precedes shifts in exchange spreads and treatment charges, and it feeds directly into cost assumptions for wiring, grid and data center construction.

finance_briefs.title: Beijing threatens retaliation after Washington sanctions two Chinese companies
finance_briefs.summary: China's commerce ministry said it strongly opposes US sanctions tied to the companies' dealings with a third party and reserves the right to take necessary measures. The exchange keeps export-control risk in the foreground for supply chains spanning semiconductors, critical minerals and industrial equipment, a recurring input for margin estimates.

politics_briefs.title: New Zealand election heads to cliffhanger with minor party positioned as kingmaker
politics_briefs.summary: National and Labour are running neck and neck with no coalition expected to secure a majority, leaving a minor party to decide the next government. For markets, the outcome shapes fiscal spending, foreign investment screening and the pace of Reserve Bank policy normalization. Coalition talks may take days, so headline risk persists into next week.

politics_briefs.title: Paraguay's president impeached and placed under house arrest after bank collapse
politics_briefs.summary: Santiago Pena was ousted over a banking crisis that left millions unable to access their money. The removal of a sitting president via impeachment is a rare event in the region and raises questions about deposit guarantees, sovereign funding costs and the legal status of bank creditors. Watch for currency pressure and any capital controls.

politics_briefs.title: Bomb threats and cyberattacks across Europe raise pressure on corporate resilience
politics_briefs.summary: A cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems, bomb threats against aircraft and software vulnerabilities have put European officials on edge, with governments urging stockpiling and continuity planning. The incidents carry direct operational risk for retailers and logistics operators and reinforce spending on industrial control security and insurance. Attribution remains unsettled, and claims of state backing are unconfirmed.

editor_note: The midterm-to-megacap transmission channel is the story of the week. Treat single-day AI index moves as positioning noise until capex guidance actually changes. Metals coverage here is about physical flows and reserve behavior, not price targets. All figures are as reported by the cited sources.

watchlist.rationale: Alphabet is the most complete bearish setup on the list. Price at 284.78 sits below all three moving averages - SMA20 317.44, SMA50 332.93 and SMA200 339.51 - forming a bearish stack, and the SMA50 has crossed below the SMA200 (death cross). RSI14 at 29.9 is in oversold territory, the weakest large-cap reading in this candidate set. The stock is 30.31% below its 52-week high but 5.2% above its 52-week low; the modest +0.78% one-day and +1.77% five-day gains are small against that structure.

JD.com is the momentum leader in this set. Price at 29.11 is up 13.36% over five days and 1.64% on the day, clearing all three averages - SMA20 26.56, SMA50 26.88 and SMA200 28.55 - and standing only 15.13% below its 52-week high. RSI14 at 72.0 is the only overbought reading across the entire candidate list, flagging short-term extension risk even as trend structure improves. MACD at 0.2440 versus signal -0.1586 produces a positive histogram near +0.40, confirming a fresh golden cross. The setup is bullish on trend and momentum, but the overbought RSI means the reading is stretched rather than early.

The dollar index shows the cleanest bullish moving-average stack among the candidates. At 102.28, price sits above SMA20 101.97, SMA50 101.09 and SMA200 99.70 for a full bullish alignment, and is only 0.65% below its 52-week high while sitting 7.04% above its 52-week low. RSI14 at 59.0 is firm but not overbought. MACD at 0.1525 versus signal 0.2254 yields a slightly negative histogram of about -0.073, so momentum is flattening even as trend structure holds. The five-day change is +0.39% and the one-day +0.72%. Trend classification is bullish; momentum is cooling.

Nvidia is a broken-momentum setup. Price at 186.64 is 8.8% lower over five days despite a +2.78% single-day bounce, and trades below SMA20 211.55, SMA50 219.81 and SMA200 204.67 - roughly 12% under the 20-day and 9% under the 200-day. RSI14 at 30.8 is on the edge of oversold, the lowest large-cap reading after GOOGL in this list. MACD at -8.2375 versus signal -5.0407 leaves a histogram near -3.20, so bearish momentum is still widening. The stock is 23.31% below its 52-week high yet still 13.62% above its 52-week low, so the drawdown is deep without being a full reset.

Ethereum is the neutral case: mixed signals rather than a resolved trend. Price at 2240.93 holds above SMA200 2155.81 but below SMA20 2323.59 and SMA50 2491.26, so the intermediate structure remains corrective. MACD at -59.2373 has crossed above its signal at -60.5943 - a golden cross with a modestly positive histogram near +1.36 - an early stabilization signal rather than a trend change. RSI14 at 40.2 is weak-neutral, and a five-day change of -0.35% alongside a +0.26% one-day move shows no thrust. ETH is 38.71% below its 52-week high.
